messages.subject: figs,
parts:
Hi,

I am thankful for Eric's comment below which cleans up a mis-conception, and
leads us into digital scientific progress:

I think it's an open secret that DS and other packages (this includes GIS,
S-PLUS, R) often just give you the (statistically correct) RAW figure, to be
brushed up further elsewhere (e.g. Adobe, Corel Draw and even Powerpoint).
Re-running or re-assembling the fig elsewhere is another option certainly
(as described below).

I am very grateful to the DS programmers, and others, that they actually
allow for a plain copy-paste, WMF (un-group'able), jpg or similar from their
software, and then I can do with it whatever I want for creating high
quality figures for publications elsewhere.

This includes imports into Word, LATEX, OpenOffice, html and xml.

In other words, one still needs a graphic designer (or similar skills) for a
good presentation, but that's what old-fashioned hardcopy publishing still
is about. That will soon diminish.

Instead, I envision a (science) world where we do NOT NEED brushed-up figs
anymore, and just add the entire DS project file to our paper (or Metadata;
I shall come back to that topic at a later date re. DS).
People can assess the entire story that way then, see raw data, and re-run
the entire thing for their own judgment. Increases trust in the findings.

I certainly think that this should become a legal requirement for policies,
such as the Marine Mammals Act, ESA etc.

For those of you that find this futuristic, or 'unrealistic' even, please
see the DIS (Data Information Service) of the International Polar Year
http://ipydis.org/ for starters(with over 60 countries signed on to it;
likely your country has as well).

NSF, NIH, CODATA, ICSU, the RIO Convention, Budapest & Berlin Declarations
etc etc all push for these concepts these days (even the EU by now; but not
the Russian government though).

Time will come.

Very best
F.

Falk Huettmann PhD, Assistant Professor
-EWHALE lab- Biology and Wildlife Dept., Institute of Arctic Biology

-----Original Message-----
From: Wildlife abundance estimation using distance sampling techniques.
[mailto:DISTANCE...@JISCMAIL.AC.UK] On Behalf Of Eric Rexstad
Sent: Tuesday, February 12, 2008 11:29 PM
To: DISTANCE...@JISCMAIL.AC.UK
Subject: Re: [DIST-SAMP] Changing fonts of axes in Distance output graphs?

Danielle/List:

If you are interested in making sophisticated plots of your detection
function (I define sophisticated to include the tiling approach you
describe), I would not employ the cut-and-paste graphics approach, but
rather I would move to another piece of software. Export the data (not
the graphic) of your detection function to another package (See
"Exporting CDS results from analysis details results" in Chapter 8 of
the users guide).

You can then send the data to Excel (see macro on the support page of
the Distance website), or recreate the graphic in R (using a script also
found in Chapter 8 of the users guide). Using Excel or R, you have
utter and complete control of every aspect of the graph (not just the
fonts, but line widths, etc. etc.)

Let me know if you need more of a boost than that.

that
